title: Practical Inference Commitment — Messaging Brief
summary: A concise internal brief positioning Redwood as the practical, operator-focused inference platform that trades model fetishism for predictable economics and operational resiliency.
one_liner: Redwood: The inference runtime teams rely on to make LLM features predictable, affordable, and resilient in production.
mission_statement: Make high-performance, reliable LLM inference accessible to every engineering team by treating inference as an operational contract, not a research prototype.
thesis: As models proliferate, production differentiation shifts to predictable serving. Teams win with engineering-first inference that exposes clear cost, latency, and reliability tradeoffs and automates common operator work.
key_pillars: Operational contract: SLAs, predictable capacity, transparent unit economics.
Developer ergonomics: same API across hosted/dedicated/private, quick onboarding, strong SDKs.
Cost control: batching, caching, quantization guidance tied to observable metrics.
Failure tolerance: automated fallbacks, regional routing, graceful degradation modes.
Observability & guardrails: token-level cost, rollout controls, alerting on quality regressions.
target_audiences: Product and ML engineers at AI-first startups
SaaS product teams adding LLM features under latency/SLA constraints
competitive_landscape_notes: Competitors either offer model access without operational guarantees or infra tooling without a developer-friendly API. Redwood's edge is marrying a high-throughput runtime with opinionated serving primitives and economics-driven controls. Watch vendors focusing on cheapest model endpoints and hyperscalers pushing managed endpoints as commoditized services.
messaging_hooks: 'Inference as a contract'—talk SLAs and unit economics, not model spec sheets.
'Ship fast, stay predictable'—onboard in hours, measure costs per feature, scale within predictable latency bands.
'Reduce surprise spend'—actionable knobs to trim token costs tied to real metrics and rollout policies.
'Keep apps online'—fallbacks to cheaper variants and region-based routing for outages.
proposed_homepage_lead: Deliver LLM features with predictable latency and transparent costs. Redwood is the inference runtime that lets engineering teams ship, measure, and control model-driven features in production.
proof_points: Hosted benchmarks: 95th percentile latency across conversational workloads under 150 ms for small-medium seq lengths.
Customer story (beta): fintech startup reduced inference cost by 40% after enabling prefix caching and recommended batching.
Dedicated SLA: 99.9% uptime with reserved capacity and autoscale burst windows.
Optimize suggestions: automated quantization recommendations improved throughput 2.5x on internal workloads.
competitive_do_nots: Avoid attacking open-source model projects directly; focus critiques on operability and economics rather than model quality. Don't claim to be the cheapest across all workloads—highlight control over cost instead.
launch_tactics: GTM blog post with a customer case and cost/latency charts.
Engineer-focused webinar demonstrating migrations from raw model endpoints to Redwood Dedicated.
Interactive calculator on site to estimate unit economics for features.
Field sales one-pager for platform teams emphasizing SLAs and private deployment options.
key_faqs: Q: How do you compare to managed endpoints from cloud providers? A: They provide model access but rarely the ops-level bundling of SLAs, routing, and cost controls tailored to LLM workloads.
Q: Can Redwood run in our VPC/on-prem? A: Yes, private deployment options with KMS and audit logs for regulated workloads.
Q: How do rollouts and fallbacks work? A: Canary and A/B rollouts with automatic fallback to compatible variants when capacity or latency SLOs are at risk.
open_risks_and_unknowns: Pricing sensitivity: customers may prefer lower sticker prices despite higher tail cost risk.
Perception risk: framing around 'inference as an operational contract' could sound bureaucratic to startups.
Integration gaps: need clearer migration playbooks from common managed endpoints and self-hosted runtimes.
next_steps: Finalize messaging for homepage and sales one-pager by 2025-03-10.
Schedule a customer webinar for 2025-03-25 and collect three case studies.
Coordinate with engineering to produce migration guide and cost calculator by 2025-04-01.
